title: Evaluation of Acute and Long-Term Outcomes Following Endovascular Treatment of Acute proximal Deep Vein Thrombosis (ELIMINATOR)
summary:
Venous thrombosis refers to conditions where a blood clot forms in a deep vein of the leg or pelvis. These clots can be dangerous: later on, many people experience symptoms in their legs such as pain or swelling (referred to as post-thrombotic syndrome). A particular risk is that a blood clot can travel to the lungs and cause a pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening.

Normally, the blood is “thinned” with medication in such cases to prevent new clots from forming and to help the body break down the existing one. However, in recent years, new possibilities have emerged: using a thin tube (catheter), medication can be injected directly into the clot, or the clot can be mechanically removed with special devices. These methods are especially used in large and sudden-onset thromboses.

It is not yet fully clear whether these new methods are truly more effective – that is, whether they remove clots more quickly, alleviate symptoms, and prevent subsequent damage. For this reason, a study is being conducted using data from 2005 to 2024, aiming to answer the following questions:

How effective are the new procedures in improving symptoms and preventing complications such as post-thrombotic syndrome?
Are there differences in potential risks and side effects between the various methods used?
Is it possible to predict in advance which patients will particularly benefit from a specific treatment or are more likely to experience complications?
For these purposes, the study will analyze anonymized patient data from the clinic. There are no risks or benefits for the affected individuals, as this is purely a retrospective analysis.
conditions: Phlebitis and thrombophlebitis of unspecified site

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of patients with deep pelvic/leg vein thrombosis who underwent interventional treatment at the University Heart Center (UHZ) Freiburg-Bad Krozingen (Bad Krozingen campus) between 2006 and 2024

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Patients with deep pelvic or leg vein thrombosis treated at the University Heart Center (UHZ) Freiburg–Bad Krozingen (site Bad Krozingen) between 2005 and 2024
-Acute symptoms within 14 days prior to presentation
-Patients treated with catheter-based local thrombolysis and/or percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy
Exclusion criteria:
-Patients with deep arm vein thrombosis
-Patients treated conservatively
-Prior interventional treatment in the target vessel
